name: Merel Nas
bio:
Love speaks in time, and the impossibility of fully grasping its character fascinates me. In my work, I attempt to figure out what love actually is, without overmagnifying it in its charm or allowing for it to be taken for granted. By observing the relationships around me and capturing fleeting moments, I try to appease my fear of forgetfulness and finitude by expressing gratitude. The use of metaphors and spiritual references helps me to address themes beyond love, such as care, relationality, intimacy, time, and devotion. These thematic interests are translated both in my paintings, which are constructed, often slightly obscured, collaged images inhabited by my personal loves, and within the love letters I devote to them.

Currently, I am working with the setting of a beach as a narrative ground, in which the searching for seashells as a futile act becomes synonymous with the creation of time. It is this promise and spending of time I wish to emphasize as important when forming and maintaining loving relationships. The seashells also influence the approach I take when it comes to my (visual) language, in their sparkly, reflective, pearlescent-colored presence.

I see painting as a practice of care through which I embody a relationality to myself, the work itself, and the subject matter of the work. By striving for intimate closeness, I make an effort to experience concentrated time. Attempting to devote myself as completely as possible to love and thereby to try and comprehend its incomprehensibility.
